brief: A recipe manager as a transformation timeline — ingredients flow through steps and combine into the dish

dominant_strengths: Concept of cascading step cards visually suggests a transformation flow rather than a flat checklist of recipe instructions
Ingredient list with colored chips and right-aligned quantities reads cleanly and supports quick scanning
Right-side metadata panel (time, difficulty, servings, calories) is well-structured and hierarchically calm
dominant_weaknesses: Step cards overlap and clip ingredient chips ('Onion', 'Oil') destroying legibility — stacking reads as broken layout, not intentional flow
Rainbow gradient hero with floating sphere is decorative noise disconnected from a cooking metaphor; clashes with the otherwise muted palette
No visible connective tissue (arrows, lines, progress) between steps, so the 'timeline' intent is implied by overlap alone, not designed
fix_priorities: Replace overlapping cards with an explicit horizontal timeline where ingredients visibly flow from left list into each step node
Remove or replace the gradient orb with a meaningful dish illustration or live state of the recipe
Resolve chip clipping with consistent card widths and ensure all ingredient tags remain fully visible
Tighten color system: unify chip colors to a restrained palette tied to ingredient categories
rationale.norman_balance: Moderate visceral appeal from soft cards and gradient, but behavioral clarity collapses under overlapping panes and the reflective 'transformation' story is told weakly.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits — the stacked steps gesture toward a timeline, but ingredients don't visibly travel or combine, so the transformation metaphor is asserted rather than designed.
